title: File System Race Conditions and Insecure Temp Files
platform_conditions: POSIX filesystem semantics (Linux, macOS, other Unix); on Windows the same class appears via share modes rather than symlink races
security_mechanism: access() answers a question about the path, and open() acts on whatever object the path names at a later instant: between the two calls an attacker who can write the directory replaces the file with a symlink, so the privilege decision made by access() is applied to an object the attacker chose (TOCTOU). mktemp-style name construction makes the target predictable, letting the attacker pre-create it or win the race routinely rather than occasionally. Opening without O_EXCL and following symlinks by default converts the race into arbitrary file creation, truncation, or disclosure in privileged directories.

source_sink_clues.source: Directories an attacker can write (world-writable temp dirs, spool and upload paths) and file names arriving from requests that are re-checked and later reopened.
source_sink_clues.sink: access/stat followed by open/fopen on the same path; mktemp/tempnam/tmpnam; open without O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW on attacker-writable directories

tracking_guards: Check that privileged code opens with O_CREAT|O_EXCL (and O_NOFOLLOW where the name may be attacker-planted), that no access()/stat() check gates a later open of the same path (act on the fd instead: fstat, fchmod, fchown), and that temp files come from mkstemp with 0600 mode.
not_candidate_when: The file lives in a directory only the process user can write (0700), the check-and-use pair operates on an already-open fd rather than a re-resolved path, or names come from mkstemp/O_EXCL so the race cannot be won by pre-creation.
public_references: CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/59.html
SEI CERT C Coding Standard: FIO01-C (identify files via fd), POS30-C (mktemp)
